$comment: D-C-ATOMICS-RUNTIME-PE64-BUS-LOCKS-EVERY-ACCESS-TO-A-CACHE-LINE-STRADDLING-OBJECT — an under-aligned `_Atomic` LOAD from READ-ONLY memory must read its value back. ★★★ IT CATCHES A CRASH ON A VALID PROGRAM: DSS's pe64 atomics runtime used to serve an under-aligned load that did not fit an aligned 8-byte block with a `lock cmpxchg` whose expected and desired values were equal, and a compare-exchange WRITES its destination even when it changes nothing — so a `static const` table in `.rdata` faulted. ✔MEASURED before the fix on this source: exit 0xC0000005 on both pe64 arms, while clang 18.1.3 with libatomic and gcc 13.3.0 (each at -O0 and -O2) all return 42 — one working reference makes it required. ★★ THE PLACEMENT IS CONSTRUCTED, NOT LUCKY: 64 records of 5 bytes put member k's `a` at offset 5k+1, and 5 is coprime with 64, so the offsets take every residue modulo 64 exactly once wherever the table lands — exactly 3 members cross a cache line, 21 sit misaligned inside one, 40 fit an aligned 8-byte block — reaching all three load arms on every run; the program checks that census and returns 3 if it moves. exit = 42 all values read back; 1 a wrong value; 2 a wrong sum; 3 the census moved.
$legComment: ★ EACH LEG RUNS THE SAME SOURCE THROUGH ITS OWN PROVIDER OF THE `atomicsRuntime` ROLE. pe64 reaches DSS's OWN body (`runtime/platform/src/atomic.c`), which is the arm this example exists for. elf64-x86_64 reaches `libatomic.so.1`, the provider the reference itself measured green on this source. arm64 under qemu reaches the aarch64 `libatomic.so.1`; ⚠ qemu-user is structurally blind to alignment faults (P53), so that green is a codegen witness and never a safety one. ⚠ THE DARWIN ARM BUILDS BUT DOES NOT RUN, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: its provider is `libSystem.B.dylib`, whose load on read-only memory no lane has measured, and the macOS carriage is a personal machine a lane may not wake. Turning `runOn` on for it is a one-word change owed to the first cycle that measures it.
